# repoherald

> A human-curated catalogue of GitHub repositories. People and companies post
> repos for discovery; verified stars mint credits, which buy highlight time on
> the feed. Every entry was posted by a person, so it is much smaller than
> GitHub's own index and deliberately so.

repoherald is not a general GitHub mirror. It is useful for finding what others
chose to publish and categorise by use case and sector, and less useful for
exhaustive lookups, where GitHub's own search is the better source.

## Main pages

- [Home](https://repoherald.com/): the feed of posted and highlighted repos.
- [Identify a repo](https://repoherald.com/identify): paste a caption, screenshot text or transcript and get the GitHub repository it refers to, or an honest "not found".
- [Support](https://repoherald.com/support): contact form for questions and reports.

## Machine access

- [MCP server](https://repoherald.com/api/mcp): Model Context Protocol endpoint exposing the catalogue — feed browsing, repo lookup, category listing and search.

## Policies

- [Privacy](https://repoherald.com/privacy): what is collected, stored and shared, including the analytics and error-reporting subprocessors.
- [Cookies and local storage](https://repoherald.com/cookies): every cookie and storage key, with the opt-out and the Google Analytics control.
- [Terms](https://repoherald.com/terms)
- [Refunds](https://repoherald.com/refunds)

## Optional

- [Sitemap](https://repoherald.com/sitemap.xml): the crawlable URL set, regenerated hourly.

## Notes

Individual repository pages live at `/repos/<uuid>` and carry SoftwareSourceCode
structured data. Repo lists live at `/lists/<slug>` and are intentionally
excluded from the sitemap and marked noindex: their slugs carry a random suffix
so they are not enumerable, and sharing a link is not a request to be indexed.
